rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states several distinct outcomes that each end in a report to a different recipient or authority, and the reporting wording is the same or nearly the same across those outcomes: Create one bpmn:endEvent per distinct outcome. Build each end event's xs:ID from the specific recipient and condition that outcome represents, not from the shared reporting wording. Before finishing, check every id attribute in the model, including those of end events, tasks, gateways and sequence flows, and make sure no id value appears more than once.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states several distinct outcomes that each end in a report to a different recipient or authority, and the reporting wording is the same or nearly the same across those outcomes

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description makes the reporting deadline or the recipient of an event depend on a sequence of yes/no checks on that event (for example whether it was fatal, whether it meets a stated severity or duration threshold, and whether another party already received a report), and each check changes the next step: Model each check as its own exclusive gateway, placed in the order the description gives the checks. Give each gateway one labelled outgoing flow per outcome, using the condition wording from the description. Attach each outcome flow to the report or step it triggers, including any stated deadline. Route the not-taken outcome to the next check or to its own continuation. Do not replace these checks with a task that assesses the event, and do not drop a check because its outcome only changes a deadline.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description makes the reporting deadline or the recipient of an event depend on a sequence of yes/no checks on that event (for example whether it was fatal, whether it meets a stated severity or duration threshold, and whether another party already received a report), and each check changes the next step

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description attaches to one occurrence a reporting duty and then a further reporting duty that it introduces as applying independently of the first, each with its own check, recipient or deadline: Model each duty as its own branch that leaves the occurrence separately. Place that duty's checks and its report task on its own branch, in the order the description gives. Do not nest the second duty behind the first duty's report, check or deadline, and do not let one gateway join the checks of both duties. Attach any stated time limit to the report task it governs.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description attaches to one occurrence a reporting duty and then a further reporting duty that it introduces as applying independently of the first, each with its own check, recipient or deadline

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description attaches a reporting duty with its own deadline or recipient to a subset of occurrences defined by a stated outcome, and a general duty to report the same occurrences also applies: Model an exclusive gateway whose question states the outcome condition in the description's own terms, not the actor's status or another condition. Place the subset's report task on the branch where that outcome holds, labelled with the stated recipient and deadline. Label the general report task with the duty's own recipient and timing as the description states them, and do not replace the outcome condition with the actor's role in any label.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description attaches a reporting duty with its own deadline or recipient to a subset of occurrences defined by a stated outcome, and a general duty to report the same occurrences also applies

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description makes the time limit or the target of a follow-up action depend on a sequence of yes/no checks applied to the same subject, where each check's result changes the next step: Model each check as its own exclusive gateway, placed in the order the description gives the checks. Give each gateway one labelled outgoing flow per outcome, using the condition wording from the description. Attach each outcome flow to the action or step it triggers, including any stated time limit. Connect the not-taken outcome to the next check or to its own continuation. Do not replace these checks with a single task that assesses the subject, and do not omit a check merely because its outcome only changes a time limit.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description makes a notification to an authority depend on several yes/no checks applied to the same occurrence, such as the stated outcome, a stated cover or status of the affected party, and whether the event was already reported to another authority, and the description joins two or more of these checks in one sentence

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a reporting duty for an occurrence, and then states that a subset of the same occurrence (defined by a stated outcome) must be reported again with its own shorter deadline even though it has already been reported: Model the general report and the repeat report as two separate tasks in sequence. Place the repeat report after the general report, on the branch of an exclusive gateway whose question states the outcome condition in the description's own terms. Label each task with only its verb, object and recipient as the description names them. Record the repeat report's own deadline and its 'even if already reported' qualification in the documentation of that task, and do not place the outcome condition or the deadline in either task label.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a reporting duty for an occurrence, and then states that a subset of the same occurrence (defined by a stated outcome) must be reported again with its own shorter deadline even though it has already been reported
